content.text: [Sat 2026-05-09 06:14 UTC] Create a script that archives the contents of the /etc/ and /home/ directories.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

# archive_etc_home.sh
# Creates compressed archives of /etc and /home.
# Output directory defaults to ./archives (next to this script).

OUT_DIR_DEFAULT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/archives"
OUT_DIR="${1:-$OUT_DIR_DEFAULT}"

TS="$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ")"
HOST="$(hostname -s 2>/dev/null || hostname)"

mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"

ETC_OUT="$OUT_DIR/${HOST}_etc_${TS}.tar.gz"
HOME_OUT="$OUT_DIR/${HOST}_home_${TS}.tar.gz"

# Use --one-file-system to avoid unexpectedly traversing mounted filesystems.
# Use numeric owners for portability.
# Use absolute paths by changing to / then archiving etc and home.

cd /

tar --create --gzip --file "$ETC_OUT" \
  --one-file-system \
  --numeric-owner \
  --warning=no-file-changed \
  etc

tar --create --gzip --file "$HOME_OUT" \
  --one-file-system \
  --numeric-owner \
  --warning=no-file-changed \
  home

echo "Wrote: $ETC_OUT"
echo "Wrote: $HOME_OUT"

[Sat 2026-05-09 06:14 UTC] Set up an SSH tunnel to a remote server for secure data transfer.

To set up an SSH tunnel for secure data transfer, pick the tunnel type you need:

## 1) Copy files securely (often simplest; no tunnel needed)
```bash
scp /path/to/localfile user@remote.example.com:/remote/path/
# or pull from remote:
scp user@remote.example.com:/remote/path/file /path/to/localdir/
```
(Use `-r` for directories.)

## 2) Local port forwarding (access a remote service securely)
Expose a remote service (e.g., remote SSH/SFTP/HTTP on port 8080) on your local machine:
```bash
ssh -N -L 9000:127.0.0.1:8080 user@remote.example.com
```
Then connect locally to `localhost:9000` and it forwards to `remote:8080`.

## 3) Remote port forwarding (let the remote reach a local service)
Expose a local service (e.g., on your laptop port 3000) to the remote server:
```bash
ssh -N -R 9000:127.0.0.1:3000 user@remote.example.com
```
Now on the remote server, connecting to `localhost:9000` reaches your local `3000`.

## 4) SOCKS proxy (general secure browsing / arbitrary TCP via proxy)
```bash
ssh -N -D 1080 user@remote.example.com
```
Set your app/browser proxy to SOCKS5 `127.0.0.1:1080`.

### Practical flags you’ll likely want
- Run in background after auth: `-f`
- Keepalive: `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=3`
- Compression (sometimes helps): `-C`
- Use a key: `-i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519`

Example (background local forward):
```bash
ssh -f -N -L 9000:127.0.0.1:8080 -o ServerAliveInterval=30 user@remote.example.com
```

This environment doesn’t have `systemctl`, so I can’t install/enable real systemd timer units here. If your machine uses systemd, create these two unit files:

### 1) Service unit
`/etc/systemd/system/archive-etc-home.service`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Archive /etc and /home

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/root/.openclaw/workspace/archive_etc_home.sh /var/backups/archives
```

### 2) Timer unit (daily)
`/etc/systemd/system/archive-etc-home.timer`
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Run archive-etc-home daily

[Timer]
OnCalendar=daily
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

### Enable + start
```bash
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now archive-etc-home.timer
systemctl list-timers --all | grep archive-etc-home
```

[Sat 2026-05-09 06:15 UTC] Verify that the data is successfully transferred to the remote storage.

To verify the archives actually made it to remote storage, do these checks on **local** and **remote**, and compare.

## 1) Confirm the local archives exist (and note sizes + hashes)
```bash
ls -lh /var/backups/archives/
sha256sum /var/backups/archives/*.tar.gz | tail -n 5
```

## 2) Confirm the files exist on the remote (size check)
If you transferred with `scp`/`rsync`, list the destination directory on the remote:
```bash
ssh user@remote.example.com 'ls -lh /remote/path/'
```

## 3) Verify integrity end-to-end (hash match)
### Option A (recommended): compare SHA-256 hashes
Local:
```bash
sha256sum /var/backups/archives/*.tar.gz > /tmp/local_archives.sha256
```
Remote (compute remote hashes):
```bash
ssh user@remote.example.com 'sha256sum /remote/path/*.tar.gz' > /tmp/remote_archives.sha256
```
Compare:
```bash
diff -u /tmp/local_archives.sha256 /tmp/remote_archives.sha256
```
No output from `diff` = hashes match = transfer is correct.

### Option B: test the tarballs on the remote without extracting
```bash
ssh user@remote.example.com 'gzip -t /remote/path/*.tar.gz'
```
And optionally:
```bash
ssh user@remote.example.com 'tar -tzf /remote/path/<onefile>.tar.gz | head'
```

## 4) If using rsync, use its built-in verification mode
```bash
rsync -av --checksum /var/backups/archives/ user@remote.example.com:/remote/path/
```
